nodes.name: AT List Tables
nodes.notes: The client base's schema, once, BEFORE any paid call. Companies and the Signals mirror are resolved from it; nothing is created here, the columns are checked by the helper Insert domains to Clayroots.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Find-Companies-Table.js

nodes.name: Get Signal Mirror Row
nodes.notes: Candidate rows in the client base's Signals mirror for this Hub signal, fetched by LOWER(TRIM({Name})) = the signal's name, built upstream by Find Companies Table (2026-09-02: the former match was a synced Record ID column that no client base carries, so every signal died here). The query is permissive on purpose, LOWER and TRIM letting whitespace and case variants through as candidates, because Airtable's = is otherwise exact and case-sensitive (probed live). Resolve Mirror Row then does the strict exact, case-sensitive, client-scoped match and refuses anything but exactly one row, before any paid call. No fields restriction: a fields list naming Client would 422 on a mirror without that column. Companies.Signals links to the mirror row id, never to the Hub row.

nodes.name: Resolve Mirror Row

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Resolve-Mirror-Row.js

nodes.notes: Refuses before any paid call when the mirror row is missing.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Filter-Qualify-Reviews.js

nodes.name: DiscoLike BizData
nodes.notes: One call per qualified company, paced 4.5 s apart: DiscoLike allows 5 requests a minute base, 15 on the Team plan, and the ceiling is per key, so every DiscoLike node in the estate holds the same interval (was 2100, about 28 a minute). fullResponse + neverError: Company Facts reads the status and classifies a miss (404) vs an error, which is why this node does not carry retryOnFail. Nothing here throws, so nothing would retry; a 429 lands in the run row as a failure with its reason instead of being silently swallowed.

nodes.notes: One task for the whole list (DiscoLike rule). BYOK: the Operator's LLM key, no platform charge.
